correctness.rationale: The assigned theorem covers r>=1 and each nonnegative pendant count a_i, with unique shortest paths in the represented finite caterpillar. Partition selected sets by zero, one or at least two occupied backbone branches. A single occupied star branch contributes F_i=(1+z)^{a_i}+z+a_i z^2, including singleton spine and each spine–leaf pair. For distinct occupied extrema i<j, selecting a spine center at an interior position would place it on a geodesic between selected extreme vertices, and a spine center at either extreme may be selected only alone within its branch. Thus the extreme factors are E_i=(1+z)^{a_i}-1+z and E_j, while interior branches independently provide A_k=(1+z)^{a_k}. No selected leaf can be internal to a path, and no allowed selected spine center lies internally on another selected-pair path: these facts establish sufficiency and necessity, not merely a one-way count. The disjoint sum yields exactly 1-r+sum_i(F_i)+sum_{i<j}E_i E_j prod_{i<k<j}A_k. Keeping the running prefix sum H_{j+1}=E_j+A_j H_j and P_j=P_{j-1}+F_j-1+E_j H_j proves the recurrence, including r=1 and a_i=0. Multiplication by degree-a_j binomial polynomials gives O(N^2) coefficient operations and O(N) coefficient memory, not bit complexity. Fresh independent BFS shortest-path enumeration of all 992 profiles (1<=r<=5,0<=a_i<=3,N<=13; 2,806,538 subsets) agreed with the symbolic formula; the two claimed seven-vertex degree-sequence twins also matched. These finite checks support but do not constitute the all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: Published broom and uniform-comb identities of Iršič et al. (2024) and the later uniform comb/corona cases of Rather (2026) are strict specializations. Iršič et al.'s general inclusion–exclusion identity presupposes a maximal general-position set classification and does not itself give this explicit full-profile formula. The fully inspected Resultary spider result assumes one branching center, unlike arbitrarily many caterpillar branch points. A current full-text survey and targeted queries under caterpillar, hairy path and generalized comb aliases did not reveal an equivalent dominating result. The four separate comparisons and exact source inspections are included below; this is best-of-knowledge priority with explicit unindexed-literature risks, not a novelty certificate.
residual_risks: Best-of-knowledge originality only: a historical unindexed equivalent result for hairy paths, heterogeneous combs or general-tree polynomial dynamic programming could exist.
The Anand et al. 2018 article was inspected at abstract level only; it cannot be used for a whole-text noncoverage conclusion.

value.rationale: The complete general-position polynomial on an arbitrary heterogeneous caterpillar is a natural exact invariant of a broad canonical tree class extending named published broom and comb cases. Its coefficients depend on the positions and multiplicities of branching along the spine and require accounting for interacting occupied extrema, not a parameter renaming. The finite all-subset classification gives a reusable O(N^2) arithmetic recurrence for every profile. The degree-matched seven-vertex pair with different polynomials demonstrates information unavailable from the degree multiset alone. No general tree, unimodality or asymptotic theorem is claimed or needed for this motivated exact enumeration to have mathematical value.

limitations: Proof only for ordinary general-position sets in finite undirected caterpillar trees; no claim for all trees or graph products.
Complexity counts integer coefficient operations, not bit complexity.
No claim about log-concavity/unimodality or full maximal-general-position-set classification.
Published broom/comb and spider special cases are prior coverage, not original by themselves.
